INSTAT's annual report of the 2025 Enquete Modulaire et Permanente aupres des Menages (EMOP), a national household survey, was published; the excerpt reports household mobile-phone ownership of 88.1% in 2025 and national, poor and non-poor breakdowns.

The bulletin states INSTAT published the 2025 annual report of the EMOP household survey in the second quarter of 2026, with consumption spending of 10,276 billion FCFA in 2025 and a poverty and consumption profile nationally and by region; the bulletin gives no exact release date, so its publication date is used.
The report states the EMOP 2025 used the fifth general population and housing census (RGPH-5), carried out in 2022, as its sampling frame; no month is given for the count.

INSTAT, with Statistics Sweden, published the synthesis report of the first pass (January-March 2025) of the EMOP household survey: 12,945 of 15,438 sampled households surveyed (83.9 per cent), results representative nationally and by region and urban/rural, with weak coverage in Kidal, Menaka and Nara for insecurity. Dated to the document's published month, as it gives no release date.

INSTAT's Q4 2025 bulletin reports validation, on 16-18 December 2025 in Bamako, of the Directory of Localities of Mali produced from RGPH5 data, so the fifth general population census has been counted; the bulletin gives no enumeration date, so the bulletin's published date is used.

INSTAT made public in November 2025 the synthesis report of the third round of the 2025 EMOP household survey (12,938 households nationwide, fieldwork July-September 2025), with a national morbidity rate of 24.4% and household consumption spending of 2,722.9 billion FCFA a quarter.

The bulletin lists the final report of the seventh Demographic and Health Survey (EDS VII), published by INSTAT in Q4 2025, with stunting among under-5s and anaemia among women 15-49 as indicators; no month is given.

The 2020-2024 statistical master plan budgets continued census cartography (poursuite de la cartographie censitaire) and the RGPH5 enumeration for 2020, with resources still to be mobilised from partners.
